tickets.note: Here's what I like. Hutchinson wins on the back line of the end zone, and that's the line you wanna win on — he's got hands like a couple of buckets.

tickets.name: Bell Cow
tickets.note: Oh, boy. Irving gets his work down in the red zone, where it's tight, and it's nasty, and I love it — he goes through you, not around you.

tickets.name: Goal Line Back
tickets.note: Jeanty is right there when they get to goal-to-go, and goal-to-go is where touchdowns happen. He puts his head down, whap, somebody's going backwards.

tickets.name: First Read
tickets.note: Now watch this guy. Gainwell doesn't need a short field, he brings his own — he runs like he's late for supper.

season.note: VALUEREPLAY-2026-09-29. Owner: "update the football ledger with the new model version and board" -> "cant backtest it?". Every committed slate 09-09..09-27 re-run through the CURRENT pipeline (nfl_mock -> nfl_value VALUESINGLES -> nfl_draft_cli, depth chart as of each date, history model as-of each date, prices as posted in slates/<date>/prices.json) and graded off nflverse pbp (td_player_id; weekly-roster status != ACT = void). 09-28 is the live board as posted and reproduced exactly by the replay. No injury report in the replay (ESPN has no archive), so a man ruled out that week is voided rather than skipped. The posted record (moons + old singles, -30.39u) is kept in nfl_season_actual.json and is not displayed. Rules were chosen on these same nine slates, so this is in-sample. FTDREPLAY/FTDSTATS-2026-09-29 (owner: "backtest the first td into the ledger" -> "stop trying to predict based on price"): 🚨 Opening Drive replayed on the same ten slates with nfl_ftd.pick_stats -- one man a slate, the highest first-TD chance from nflverse football alone (usage, red-zone share, TD rate, position, home, offence vs defence TDs/EPA/opening-drive TDs; fit 2019-2025), graded on each game's first touchdown. Only the UNITS use a price, and first-TD prices were never archived, so they are ESTIMATED from the archived anytime price with the PIT@CLE markup curve. Research: claude/ftdstats-2026-09-29.md.

ftd.rule: FTDSTATS-2026-09-29: one man a slate, the highest first-TD chance from football alone (nfl_ftd_stats.py); no price in the choice
ftd.price_curve: units at FTD implied = split x (0.997 - 0.063 ln split), from the PIT@CLE first-TD board

ftd.name: Pop the Cork
ftd.note: Christian McCaffrey to score the first touchdown of LV at SF. Here's what I like about McCaffrey. First drive, they give him the ball, and they give him the ball, and when they get down close, whap, they give him the ball again. That's football!
